acceptance_criteria: Device discovery and collection succeeds without TRUST_ENTRY_MISSING
SSH Host Key trust is properly established

baseline.observed: Adding a device fails with connect_failed: host_key_rejected: TRUST_ENTRY_MISSING
baseline.what_exists: SSH trust is missing or failing to be recorded during discovery

invariants: No security weakening (do not disable strict host key checking globally)
report.objective: Fix the TRUST_ENTRY_MISSING error when adding/discovering a device. Ensure the host key is properly fetched and stored in DeviceTrustRepository during the discovery phase.
requirements: Fix the TRUST_ENTRY_MISSING error on device discovery and collection.

changed: Single-device enrollment now presents the same security-admin trust action as management-server discovery.
Added a regression test for trust authorization availability before direct enrollment.
completed: Exposed the existing explicit SSH trust authorization flow in the direct Check Point device-enrollment form.
Reused the persisted, endpoint-scoped authorization endpoint; no trust-on-first-use behavior was added.

effects.ui: The direct Check Point enrollment form now includes SSH trust authorization.

integration.merge_decision: PO controlled; no push or PR created.

next.objective: Authorize the independently verified SSH host key, then retry direct enrollment or collection against the target device.

preserved: Strict SSH host-key verification, explicit independent verification, and audited persistence.
unresolved_risks: A security administrator must independently verify and authorize the endpoint key before the next device connection; automatic trust would violate the frozen contract.
